# Sync the docs with the code

Scope: $ARGUMENTS

Follow `.claude/rules/how-to-use-sdlc-docs.md`. Edit only `CLAUDE.md` and files in `docs/sdlc/`.

## 1. Find what changed

- If a starting point was given, use `git log --stat <since>..HEAD` and `git diff --stat <since>..HEAD`.
  Otherwise use the date in each doc's most recent INFERRED marker, or the last 30 commits.
- If this isn't a git repository, compare the docs with the current code directly.
- Group the changes: new or moved folders, new or changed endpoints and data models, new dependencies or
  versions, changed build, run or deploy commands, new environments or configuration.

## 2. Update the docs

| Change | Doc to check |
|---|---|
| Folders, entry points, new kinds of files | `docs/sdlc/01-folder-structure.md` |
| Stack, versions, scope | `docs/sdlc/00-project-overview.md` |
| Build, run and test commands | `CLAUDE.md` |
| Modules and how they connect | `docs/sdlc/03-architecture.md` (if it exists) |
| Endpoints, data model, integrations | `docs/sdlc/06-api-and-data.md` (if it exists) |
| Setup, environments, configuration | `docs/sdlc/05-environments-and-setup.md` (if it exists) |

- Rewrite sections marked INFERRED when they're out of date, and update the marker's date.
- Never change text a person wrote. If it's outdated, list it with the suggested new wording.
- Keep the files short; remove inferred content that no longer applies.

## 3. Report

A list of doc · what changed, then the suggested edits to human-written sections for the user to accept or
reject.
